item.title: North’s pride | Navatu Secondary praises new policy

item.content:encoded:
THE Navatu Secondary School under-19 team, the lone northern school competing in this Saturday’s Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Vodafone Super Deans Championship, has hailed the organisers for introducing a game-changing registration policy.

The new rule allows teams to bolster their squads by recruiting up to six additional players of the same age grade from neighbouring schools within their zone, giving schools like Navatu a much-needed boost ahead of the crucial eliminations and finals.

Navatu Secondary earned their spot in the quarter-finals with a hard-fought 19-12 victory over a spirited Queen Victoria School side at Ratu Ganilau Park last Saturday.

This weekend, they’re set to host Suva Grammar School in what promises to be another thrilling clash on home turf.

Head coach Alipate Ravulo spoke passionately about how the policy is a lifeline for northern schools, which often struggle with smaller student numbers compared to their rivals in other zones.

“We’re incredibly thankful for this change in registration rules. Before, northern schools were at a real disadvantage because we simply don’t have the student roll or player depth like other zones do,” he said.

“This new rule has been a game-changer for small schools. There are some fantastic players in schools that didn’t make it through to the playoffs, and bringing in four such players has made a real difference.” Navatu U19 have registered players from Napuka Secondary and Bucalevu Secondary School. The side will take on Suva Grammar School at Ratu Ganilau Park in Savusavu this Saturday at 11.30am in their U19 super Deans quarterfinals.

Meanwhile in the U18 grade quarterfinals fixtures at HFC Bank National Stadium in Suva, Lelean Memorial School will battle Ratu Navula College at 4.30 pm followed by Suva Grammar School taking on Ba Provincial Institute at 5.55pm. At Garvey Park in Tavua, Ra High School will take on defending champion Ratu Kadavulevu School at 1.40pm followed by Cuvu College who will battle Nasinu Secondary School at 3.05pm.

item.title: Fainu brothers’ bid to play for Fiji denied

item.content:encoded:
THE Fainu brothers have been ruled ineligible to represent Fiji at the Rugby League world cup after failing to meet the International Rugby League’s eligibility requirements. Wests Tigers trio Samuela, Sione and Latu Fainu had sought to play for Fiji through their grandmothers’ heritage but were unable to provide accredited documentation to support their claim.

International Rugby League (IRL) chair Troy Grant said the governing body had no concerns about the brothers’ desire to play for Fiji but was bound by its eligibility regulations.

“All three are eligible to play for Tonga and New Zealand but believe they have Fijian heritage that they wish to honour,” Grant said.

“Unfortunately, they have been unable to establish it with accredited records from Fiji.”

Grant said the IRL had extended the time frame for the players to provide supporting documents, but the required evidence had not been produced.

“The IRL has no issues with their application or desire to play for Fiji as it’s evident, they have a genuine desire to play for Fiji,” he said.

“The IRL has rigid eligibility criteria and has given them more time to provide credible documents to support their application.”

The brothers had been included in Fiji’s 40-member preliminary squad for the Rugby League World Cup alongside Mark Nawaqanitawase, Api Koroisau, Jahream Bula and Sunia Turuva.

The absence is a setback for Fiji as the Bati finalises its squad for the world cup later this year, with selectors now expected to look elsewhere to fill the vacant positions.

item.title: Ballu praises Team Fiji
item.description: THE 2026 Commonwealth Games Team Fiji Chef de Mission Ajay Ballu believes the nation’s young squad has laid a strong foundation for future international success despite finishing 20th on the medal standings at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. item.content:encoded:
THE 2026 Commonwealth Games Team Fiji Chef de Mission Ajay Ballu believes the nation’s young squad has laid a strong foundation for future international success despite finishing 20th on the medal standings at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

Ballu said the team exceeded expectations by winning a gold and a bronze medal against more experienced opposition that included Olympians and former Commonwealth champions.

“I think we did really well, considering we took a very young team,” Ballu said. “Competing against athletes with Olympic and Commonwealth experience has given our athletes an understanding of the level they need to reach. They know where they have to be now.”

He praised the weightlifting team’s record-breaking performances by gold medalist Taniela Rainibogi, saying the national and Commonwealth records achieved in Glasgow highlighted the depth of young talent emerging in the sport.

Ballu also commended Fiji’s lone female boxer for her impressive campaign, saying she had the potential to reach the gold medal bout, and her performance reflected the progress boxing has made through its growing youth development programme.

While pleased with the results, Ballu admitted the biggest challenge in Glasgow was adapting to the cold weather, along with transport arrangements that required athletes and officials to walk considerable distances between venues.

Despite the long journey to Scotland, Ballu said arriving two days early allowed the team sufficient time to acclimatise before competition. With the Commonwealth Games now over, Ballu said Team Fiji’s focus immediately shifts to next year’s Pacific Games in Tahiti, which will also serve as an important stepping stone towards the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games. He challenged athletes to remain committed after a short break, revealing Fiji’s ambitious goal is to finish third at the Tahiti Pacific Games before targeting first place at the 2031 Pacific Games in Tonga.

Ballu also thanked Fijians for their unwavering support throughout the Games.

“We were blessed with messages of goodwill, prayers and encouragement from back home. We thank everyone in Fiji for standing behind Team Fiji.”

item.title: Nadi backs selection process amid debate
item.description: NADI Rugby Union vice president Jeff Tamata has defended the union’s selection process following widespread discussion on social media over the composition of the Nadi men’s senior team for the Skipper Cup competition. Some supporters have questioned the selection of players during round-one match against Kadavu, claiming several standout performers from the Nadi club games competition were overlo
item.content:encoded:
NADI Rugby Union vice president Jeff Tamata has defended the union’s selection process following widespread discussion on social media over the composition of the Nadi men’s senior team for the Skipper Cup competition.

Some supporters have questioned the selection of players during round-one match against Kadavu, claiming several standout performers from the Nadi club games competition were overlooked despite strong performances during the club games season.

Tamata acknowledged the criticism but said the union remains focused on what it can control rather than online reactions.

“One thing we can’t control is how fans react, especially on social media,” Tamata said.

“We’ll take the positive out of it, work on the things that need to be addressed and move forward from there.”

He said the union has measures in place regarding activity on its official social media platforms but stressed that the team’s performances on the field would ultimately provide the best response.

“We know some fans were disappointed with some of the posts being made, but we can’t control that. We’ll control what we can, and that is our performance on the field, and let them do the talking.”

Tamata urged loyal Nadi supporters to continue backing the side as the team prepares for its second-round Skipper Cup clash against Lautoka this Saturday at Churchill Park.

He said the executives have full confidence in the current squad and the long-term direction of the union.

“We trust our system, we trust ourselves and we trust our players,” he said.

Tamata pointed to last week’s victory, where eight players made their Skipper Cup debuts, as proof the union’s faith in youth is paying off.

He also thanked the union’s sponsors, stakeholders, supporters and the Vanua for their continued backing behind the Nadi team.

Tamata added that the impressive performance of the Nadi Under-20 side last week helped set the standard for the senior team, while the union continues strengthening its administrative structures alongside its on-field ambitions.

“Our objective is to trust the system. If we keep doing the small things right, the results on the field will take care of themselves,” he said.

item.title: National schools football battle begins soon
item.description: THE stage is set for another exciting Extra Fiji Secondary Schools Football Association Championship after the official pool draws were conducted yesterday at the Fiji FA Academy in Ba. The national championship will be held at Subrail Park in Labasa from August 19-22, with more than 1,500 students, teachers and officials expected to converge on the northern town for four days of football action.
item.content:encoded:
THE stage is set for another exciting Extra Fiji Secondary Schools Football Association Championship after the official pool draws were conducted yesterday at the Fiji FA Academy in Ba.

The national championship will be held at Subrail Park in Labasa from August 19-22, with more than 1,500 students, teachers and officials expected to converge on the northern town for four days of football action.

Fiji Secondary Schools Football Association president Aminesh Ram believes this year’s tournament will be one of the most competitive in recent years, with schools from both Viti Levu and Vanua Levu determined to claim national honours.

“Approximately 1,500 athletes and teachers will converge in Labasa.

“Schools in Viti Levu are eager to take the trophies away from Vanua Levu, but the schools in Vanua Levu are saying they want to keep the trophies in the North. It will be tough matches,” Ram said.

The Open Girls competition features five pools, with defending regional powers spread across the draw. Pool A includes Central College, Rampur College, Waiqele College and Dreketi Central College, while Pool B has Tavua College, MGM High School, Korovuto College and All Saints Secondary School.

Pool C comprises Bucalevu Secondary School, Labasa College, Suva Muslim College and Nakasi High School. Pool D features Labasa Sangam College, Nadi Sangam College, Pandit Vishnu Deo Memorial College and Ba Sangam College, while Pool E includes Nukuloa College, Vunimono High School, Lekutu Secondary School and Nilsen College.

The U17 grade will see Labasa Sangam College, Nadroga Arya College, DAV College and Ba Sangam College battle in Pool A, while Vunimono High School, Penang Sangam College, Central College Lautoka and Labasa Muslim College make up Pool B.

In the U15 division, Pool A consists of AD Patel College, Nadi Sangam College, All Saints Secondary School and Vunimono High School. Pool B includes Rishikul Sanatan College, Labasa College, Central College Lautoka and Tavua College.

The U19 grade is expected to be highly competitive, with Rewa 1, Shree Guru Nanak Khalsa College and MGM High School in Pool A. Pool B features Tavua College, Vashist Muni College and All Saints Secondary School, while Pool C includes Central College, SVC, Rewa 2 and Penang Sangam College.

Pool D consists of Labasa College, Tilak High School, Xavier College and Nadi Sangam College, while Pool E brings together Suva Muslim College, Ba Sangam College, Labasa Muslim College and Labasa Sangam College.

With national titles on the line and regional pride at stake, the championship is expected to deliver intense competition as schools from across the country battle for supremacy in Labasa.

item.title: Deans: MGM’s title bid
item.description: DISCIPLINE will be a major focus for Mahatma Ghandi Memorial School’s Under-16 as the side head into this weekend’s Vodafone Super Deans Trophy national quarter-finals. Speaking ahead of this week’s clash, the team captain Wasiki Ramatakubou said preparations had gone well despite the high stakes of the competition.
item.content:encoded:
DISCIPLINE will be a major focus for Mahatma Ghandi Memorial School’s Under-16 as the side head into this weekend’s Vodafone Super Deans Trophy national quarter-finals.

Speaking ahead of this week’s clash, the team captain Wasiki Ramatakubou said preparations had gone well despite the high stakes of the competition.

“Preparation is going well. It’s the same as every other team. It’s either win or lose. It’s do or die at this stage,” Ramatakubou said.

Ramatakubou said discipline had been one of the team’s biggest concerns in previous matches and said the players had worked to improve that area during the week.

“I think discipline is one area we need to improve on. We will try our best and just take the win in this game.”

With a place in the semi-finals on the line, he said the team is focused on giving its best rather than dwelling on last year’s results.

“We’ll just try our best. Every other team wants to win but only the best can come out,” he said.

The captain expects another physical contest this weekend, saying their opponents would pose a challenge despite qualifying third from the eastern zone.

“It will be a tough game. They are also a team that wants to win, so we’ll have to do our best and make sure we don’t fumble the game.”

He also acknowledged the support of parents, school management, coaches and supporters who backed the team throughout its preparations.

Mahatma Ghandi will face Lelean Memorial School at the Bidesi grounds at 12.25pm, Saturday August 8.

item.title: FRU defends Fijiana XV timing
item.description: FIJI Rugby Union has defended the scheduling of Saturday’s Vodafone Fijiana XV Test against South Africa alongside the Vodafone Deans and Weet-Bix Raluve national quarter-finals. The decision has sparked debate among rugby fans this week. But the union says Saturday is not about choosing between the Fijiana and the Deans.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI Rugby Union has defended the scheduling of Saturday’s Vodafone Fijiana XV Test against South Africa alongside the Vodafone Deans and Weet-Bix Raluve national quarter-finals.

The decision has sparked debate among rugby fans this week. But the union says Saturday is not about choosing between the Fijiana and the Deans.

It is about celebrating the game. From the stars of today to the stars of tomorrow.

The Vodafone Fijiana XV will host South Africa in a World Rugby-sanctioned Test at HFC Bank Stadium before Fiji’s leading secondary school teams battle for places in the Deans and Raluve semi-finals.

Fiji Rugby chief executive Koli Sewabu said the occasion was bigger than one Test match.

He said it was another step in the growth of women’s rugby and a chance to inspire the next generation.

“The Vodafone Fijiana XV are not only representing Fiji this weekend, but they are also inspiring the next generation of young girls and boys who dream of wearing the white jersey,” Sewabu said. He said the day’s programme had been deliberately structured to showcase Fiji Rugby’s pathway, allowing school players to experience the atmosphere of an international Test before taking the field themselves. Board member Cathy Wong said the Test was one of the most important events on Fiji Rugby’s calendar. She said every girl watching from the stands should believe she could one day wear the Fijiana jersey.

Fiji Rugby has urged supporters to arrive early, get behind the Vodafone Fijiana XV, and stay to witness the future of Fiji rugby unfold in the Vodafone Deans and Weet-Bix Raluve national quarter-finals. Match kicks off at 2pm.

item.title: Rewa faces title holders in Round 2
item.description: REWA faces one of its toughest tests of the 2026 Skipper Cup season this weekend when it takes on defending champions Malolo in a highly anticipated Round Two clash. After suffering defeat in the opening round, the FMF Rewa will be eager to bounce back this weekend when it takes on defending champions Malolo in a highly anticipated round two clash.
item.content:encoded:
REWA faces one of its toughest tests of the 2026 Skipper Cup season this weekend when it takes on defending champions Malolo in a highly anticipated Round Two clash.

After suffering defeat in the opening round, the FMF Rewa will be eager to bounce back this weekend when it takes on defending champions Malolo in a highly anticipated round two clash.

Standing in their way is a confident Malolo outfit, which begins its title defence determined to maintain its status as the team to beat after lifting the Skipper Cup crown last season.

For Rewa, the encounter presents an opportunity to measure itself against the competition’s benchmark and prove it can compete with the country’s top provincial teams.

The match is expected to be a physical contest, with Malolo relying on the experience that carried it to last year’s championship, while Rewa will look to match the defending champions with youthful energy and determination.

Round Two also gives both sides the chance to strengthen their positions early in the competition, where every point could prove crucial in the race for the playoffs.

With confidence, momentum and valuable competition points on the line, rugby fans can expect an entertaining battle when the two teams meet this weekend.

Rewa will host Malolo at the Burebasaga grounds on Saturday, August 8 at 3pm. Other matches that will also kick off at 3pm; Navosa v Taveuni at Vatureba park, Naitasiri v Kadavu at Ratu Cakobau park, Ba v Tailevu at Govind Park in Ba, Lautoka v Nadi at Churchill park, Nadroga v Suva at Lawaqa park.
